transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Over the last month I’ve just lost interest in my art, dancing, and even my job, and I can’t seem to care about anything the way I used to. It's just been really hard to get through the day when everything feels so flat.
Have you experienced any periods of feeling better or having more interest in activities over the past month, or has it been consistently flat the entire time?

No, it's been consistently flat the entire time. It honestly feels like someone flipped a switch a month ago, and I've just been stuck in this heavy, flat state without any breaks. I haven't had any moments where I felt better or regained interest in anything.
Have you experienced episodes like this before in your life, or is this the first time you've felt this persistent lack of interest and flatness?

Actually, these swings between feeling overly revved up and then sinking into these heavy, flat lows have been happening off and on for about five months now, starting when the busy tax season ramped up. This current low stretch has been going on steadily since not long after that intense rush ended.
Can you describe the 'overly revved up' periods you mentioned, specifically how your mood, energy, and behavior were during those times, and how they differed from your normal self?

During those weeks, I had this intense energy where I only slept three or four hours a night but felt completely wired, with my thoughts racing and me talking a mile a minute. I felt so confident that I took on extra client accounts, signed up for every salsa class, and drafted plans for my own bookkeeping business. It was way faster and more intense than my normal self, like I was running on a constant buzz and couldn't slow down.

Can you estimate how long these 'revved up' periods typically last before you sink into the 'heavy, flat' lows, and do you notice any triggers or patterns that seem to precede the shift from one state to the other?

Those revved-up periods usually last for a couple of weeks, when I feel totally buzzed and barely sleep. The trigger seems to be high-stress times at work, like this past tax season when we were short-staffed and I took on too much. Once that intense rush ended, I abruptly crashed into this heavy, flat low.
Can you tell me more about how often these cycles of feeling 'revved up' and then 'heavy and flat' happen, and if there's a pattern to how long each phase lasts before switching to the other?

These swings have been going on for about five months now, ever since the tax season rush first started. That "revved up" phase only lasted for about two or three weeks, but this heavy, flat low has been dragging on steadily for almost five months since that high phase ended.

Can you clarify if these cycles of 'revved up' and 'heavy, flat' phases have been recurring regularly over the five months, or if this is more of a single episode with a long low phase, and do you recall any periods of normal mood in between these extremes?

It’s definitely been more of a single high phase followed by one long, continuous low, rather than cycling back and forth. The revved-up part lasted just a few weeks during tax season, and immediately after, I crashed into this heavy, flat feeling that has been going on steadily for about five months now. I haven't really had any periods of feeling like my normal self since this low phase started.

You mentioned the 'revved up' period lasted for a couple of weeks, but can you confirm if during that time, your mood and energy were consistently elevated for most of the day, every day, for at least 7 consecutive days, or was it more sporadic?

Yes, it was absolutely consistent every single day for those entire two weeks, not sporadic at all. It felt like a continuous wave of high energy and being buzzed that just didn't let up from morning to night. I was on the go the whole time without any breaks during that period.
Can you confirm if the current 'heavy, flat' low phase has lasted continuously for at least two weeks without any significant improvement in your mood or interest in activities?

Yes, it has lasted much longer than just two weeks. This heavy, flat feeling has been going on steadily for about five months now without any break or improvement. It just feels like one long, exhausting stretch that I can't seem to shake.
To confirm, the most recent 'revved up' episode lasted less than 4 weeks, and the current 'heavy, flat' episode has lasted more than 2 weeks, correct?

Yes, that is exactly correct. The revved-up period lasted for just about two to three weeks during the peak of tax season, while this heavy, flat feeling has been dragging on steadily for about five months now, which is much longer than two weeks.

To further clarify, you're saying the most recent 'revved up' episode lasted less than 4 weeks, but can you specify if it met the full criteria for a manic episode, such as lasting at least 7 consecutive days, or if it was shorter?

Yes, it definitely lasted for about two to three weeks straight, which is well over seven consecutive days. During those weeks, I felt consistently energized, buzzed, and barely slept every single day, rather than it just being a few short days.
Did you experience any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, during either the 'revved up' or 'heavy, flat' episodes?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I've never had any hallucinations, delusions, or anything of that nature during either my high or low periods.

You mentioned the 'revved up' period lasted for about two to three weeks, but can you confirm if, during that time, you experienced any significant impairment in social or occupational functioning, or if you required hospitalization due to the severity of your symptoms?

No, I didn't need to be hospitalized, and I actually felt highly productive and on top of the world rather than impaired. While my coworkers noticed I was talking fast and a bit snappy, I was getting a ton of work done; the actual mistakes and social withdrawal only started once I crashed into this low state.

Can you confirm whether, during your 'revved up' periods, you experienced at least three or more symptoms such as inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, more talkative than usual, flight of ideas, distractibility, increase in goal-directed activity, or excessive involvement in pleasurable activities that could lead to painful consequences?

Yes, I definitely experienced several of those. I only needed three to four hours of sleep a night without feeling tired, and my coworkers joked that I was talking a mile a minute because my thoughts were racing with so many ideas. I also had this huge wave of confidence where I took on way too many tasks at once, fully believing I could easily start my own bookkeeping firm.

Can you clarify if the symptoms during your 'revved up' period caused significant distress or impairment in your social or occupational functioning, or if they were more of a subjective experience without major consequences?

During that revved-up time, I didn't feel distressed or impaired at all—I actually felt on top of the world, extremely productive, and full of energy despite barely sleeping. While I was a bit snappy with coworkers and talked really fast, it didn't cause any major problems or consequences at the time. The real distress, mistakes at work, and pulling away from everyone only started after I crashed into this current low phase.

Did your most recent 'revved up' episode meet the full criteria for a hypomanic episode, with symptoms lasting at least four consecutive days, or did it meet the full criteria for a manic episode, lasting at least seven consecutive days, as you've described it lasting two to three weeks?

Yes, it lasted continuously for about two to three weeks, which is well over both four and seven days. During those weeks, the high energy, lack of sleep, and buzzed feeling were constant every single day. It didn't lead to hospitalization or total chaos, though, just extreme productivity and me talking really fast.

Did the symptoms during your 'revved up' period cause any significant problems in your daily life or relationships, despite feeling productive, or were they mostly well-tolerated by you and those around you?

At the time, I didn't see it as a problem because I felt incredibly productive and on top of the world. I did get pretty snappy and annoyed with coworkers who couldn't keep up with my pace, and they joked that I was talking a mile a minute like I had too much coffee. It was mostly tolerated, but looking back, I was definitely a bit overwhelming and irritable to the people around me.

You've mentioned the 'revved up' period lasted about two to three weeks, which suggests it could meet criteria for a manic episode, but you also mentioned it didn't cause significant impairment or require hospitalization. Can you confirm if, during this time, you felt like you were able to control your actions and behaviors, or if you felt like you were unable to stop or control them, even if they might have had negative consequences?

I'm not entirely sure how to answer that. During those weeks, I felt so swept up in the high energy and excitement of all my plans that I didn't really think about whether I was in control or not. It all just felt completely natural and positive at the time, rather than feeling like I was doing things I couldn't stop.

Did you experience any periods of abnormally elevated or irritable mood during the 'revved up' episode that lasted at least 7 consecutive days, and were there any periods where you felt your mood was not just elevated but also mixed with depressive symptoms simultaneously?

Yes, that buzzed and upbeat feeling lasted for a couple of weeks straight, and I definitely felt pretty snappy and irritable if anyone tried to slow me down. I didn't experience those high feelings mixed with depressive symptoms at the same time, though; it was a very distinct switch where I was either highly revved up or crashed into this heavy low.

Did the symptoms during your 'revved up' period meet the full criteria for a manic episode, which includes lasting at least 7 consecutive days and causing significant impairment, or did they more closely align with hypomanic episode criteria, which involves less severe symptoms and less impairment?

It definitely aligns more with the hypomanic description because I didn't feel impaired at all during those revved-up weeks. I felt incredibly productive, energetic, and on top of the world, even though I was barely sleeping and talking a mile a minute. The actual impairment, mistakes at work, and struggle to function only started after I crashed into my current low state.

Given that your 'revved up' periods have been less severe and didn't cause significant impairment, but have switched to long 'heavy, flat' lows, do you think the pattern of your episodes, with the recent low phase lasting about five months, suggests a more chronic condition, or do you feel like you're experiencing distinct episodes of highs and lows?

I definitely feel like these are distinct episodes of highs and lows, since that very clear 'revved up' phase during the tax rush completely flipped into this heavy, flat low. While the overall swings have been happening off and on for about five months, this current low phase has been a constant, heavy weight ever since that initial high phase ended.

Can you confirm whether the current 'heavy, flat' low phase has caused significant impairment in your social or occupational functioning, such as requiring hospitalization or causing substantial problems in your daily life or relationships?

I haven't needed to be hospitalized, but this low phase has definitely caused major problems in my daily life. At work, I've actually been pulled into meetings about my accuracy because of mistakes I never used to make, and I've completely stopped going to my salsa classes and community events. Even at home, I'm struggling just to keep up with basic chores like the dishes and laundry.

Can you clarify if the significant impairment and problems in your daily life and relationships during the current 'heavy, flat' low phase have been consistent with a major depressive episode, or if they have been less severe?

It has definitely been a severe and major disruption to my life, rather than just a mild phase. I've been pulled into meetings at work for making mistakes I never used to make, and I've completely stopped going to my salsa classes and community events. At home, I'm so exhausted that I've let the dishes pile up and I'm living out of laundry baskets because I just can't keep up.
Have you experienced at least two years of symptoms with periods of hypomanic symptoms and depressive symptoms, or has the duration of your symptoms been shorter?

No, it hasn't been two years at all. These swings between feeling overly revved up and sinking into these heavy lows have only been happening off and on for about five months, starting around the time the last tax season ramped up.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any other episodes similar to the 'revved up' and 'heavy, flat' phases you've described over the past five months, or if this is the first time you've had such distinct episodes of highs and lows?

These swings between feeling overly revved up and then sinking into these long, heavy lows have been happening off and on for about five months now, starting around when the tax season ramped up. This is the first time in my life I've ever experienced these kinds of distinct highs and lows.
Have you had any periods of at least two months where you felt completely normal, without any symptoms of being 'revved up' or 'heavy and flat', over the past five months?

No, I haven't had any periods of feeling normal over the past five months. Since that high phase ended, I've been feeling steadily down, flat, and exhausted for almost this entire stretch with absolutely no breaks. I haven't had any moments of feeling like my usual self.

Have you experienced any periods of rapid cycling, where you switched between hypomanic and depressive symptoms within the same week, or has the switch between 'revved up' and 'heavy, flat' phases taken longer, such as weeks or months?

No, I don't switch back and forth within the same week; the phases definitely last much longer than that. The "revved up" phase lasted for a few weeks during the tax rush, and this current "heavy, flat" low has been going on steadily for about a month now, within the overall pattern of swings I've had over the last five months.

Can you estimate how many episodes of 'revved up' and 'heavy, flat' phases you've experienced over the past five months, and how long each of these episodes typically lasts before switching to the other phase?

Over the last five months, there hasn't been a lot of rapid switching; it's really just been one main cycle. The "revved up" phase lasted for about two to three weeks during the busy tax season, and immediately after that ended, I crashed into this "heavy, flat" phase, which has been going on steadily for the remaining five months.

Can you confirm if you have experienced more than four episodes of major depressive, manic, or hypomanic episodes within the past 12 months, which would help differentiate between the potential diagnoses?

I'm not really sure, but I don't think I've had that many episodes. I only really remember having that one "revved up" phase during tax season and then this current low phase, which has been going on for the last five months.

Have you had any other episodes similar to the 'revved up' and 'heavy, flat' phases you've described over the past five months, prior to this period in your life, or is this the first time you've experienced such distinct episodes of highs and lows?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. These distinct highs and lows are completely new to me and only started about five months ago when the busy tax season ramped up.
